add.name: GitBisect
add.description: List the commits between a revision known good and one known bad — the candidates a bisect would narrow down, newest first. Read-only, and a genuine gap: the built-in GitStatus shows the working tree, not history. The stateful workflow (`git bisect start`, `good`, `bad`, `run`, `reset`) is several commands and belongs in Bash; this is the query that tells you what you would be bisecting. Note the two placeholders in one argument: a *required* placeholder may be embedded in a larger argument like this, while an optional one may not.

good.description: A revision known to be good — a tag, a sha, or `HEAD~10`.

bad.description: A revision known to be bad, usually the newer of the two.

add.name: GitLog
add.description: Show recent commits, newest first, at most `max` of them. `max` is required: this format cannot express an optional flag that takes a value, because dropping one would leave the flag bare.

add.name: CargoTest
add.description: Run the test suite for the current crate. Optionally filter by a substring of the test name.

filter.description: Only run tests whose name contains this substring.

add.name: CargoCheck
add.description: Type-check the current crate without producing a binary. Faster than a full build.
